name: Deer Stone Monuments and Related Bronze Age Sites
description: High on the slopes of the Khangai Ridge in central Mongolia, tall carved standing stones rise from the grassland, some as much as four metres high. Nomadic herders raised these deer stones between about 1200 and 600 BCE, and they cover them with engraved stags. They stand beside huge burial mounds and sacrificial altars, forming ceremonial landscapes of the Bronze Age steppe.
